verdict.rationale: Zapier documents issuing an agent credential: you create an MCP server and generate a connection token for the client. It also claims 'managed auth and permissions you control' and account-level restrictions, and each server carries its own tool list. That implies per-agent scoping, but the evidence never states that a token is limited to specific actions or apps. missing for 10: explicit documentation of token scope granularity (per-tool/per-app least privilege), token revocation/rotation/expiry, per-agent scoped API keys for the SDK, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Connect any MCP client to Zapier MCP by creating a server and generating a connection token, then adding it as a Bearer header or query parameter.
all with managed auth and permissions you control
Account-level restrictions, managed connections, and workspace controls apply to all of them.
